speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility; to understand the underlying cause, please tell me your exact age and when your growth spurt typically occurs. Additionally, have you noticed any fractures occurring with minimal trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency).

The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (partial labial fusion, clitoromegaly), maternal hirsutism, and subsequent virilization (acne) alongside bone fragility strongly points to this condition. I will now request the specific genetic testing and hormone panel needed to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone, 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency Gene Mutation Analysis.
